angle: Between the lake and the escarpment, a hot tub or sauna in Halton is the wellness room the house never came with: a place where the QEW commute ends, a cedar sauna leads into a cold plunge, and a tight side yard still fits the whole routine.

hot-tub.intro: Halton buyers want a tub that suits the house and the lot. Every Jacuzzi, Nordic, Aquasolus and Wellness Shop Ontario tub is running on our floor off the QEW at Guelph Line, and Red Tag pricing takes 20% off every new 2026 Jacuzzi in stock.
body: Lake Ontario keeps Burlington and Oakville a few degrees milder than Georgetown or Milton, but it also sends a damp wind across lakeshore yards from November through March, and the brow of the escarpment above Kilbride and Waterdown catches more snow and more ice. That shapes placement more than temperature does. On a lakeshore lot we angle the tub so the cabinet and cover hinge sit out of the prevailing wind, and on escarpment properties we plan for a cover that sheds ice rather than holding it. Halton soil is heavy clay, so a pad poured in October and left to cure beats one poured into a wet April thaw.

Yards here come in three kinds. Older streets in Roseland, Shoreacres, Bronte and Old Oakville have deep lots with mature trees and a garage blocking the side yard, so we often lift over the roof with a crane. New builds in Alton Village, the Orchard, north Oakville and every Milton subdivision have a gate under four feet wide and a panel in an unfinished basement near the back wall: a dolly delivery and a short electrical run. Rural Carlisle, Kilbride and Halton Hills properties have room to spare and a hydro panel two hundred feet from the ideal spot, so the electrical estimate matters as much as the tub price.

Who buys here: couples in Aldershot bungalows who want a J-335 or J-355 that heats fast and runs cheap, families in Millcroft and Glen Abbey who fill a J-485 or J-508 on Friday nights, and executives who sit on the 403 from Hamilton or the QEW from Mississauga and want the SmartTub app to have a J-445 ready when they pull in. Shift workers at Joseph Brant and Oakville Trafalgar buy tubs for recovery, not parties. Burlington, Oakville, Milton and Mississauga are on municipal water; Carlisle, Kilbride and much of Halton Hills run on wells, and we set the water care up differently for each.

faq.q: Where should a hot tub go on a lakeshore lot that gets wind off Lake Ontario?
faq.a: Put the cover hinge on the lee side so the folded cover does not act as a sail, and keep the tub within a few steps of a door you actually use in February. A cedar screen or the corner of the house cuts the wind and the heat loss that comes with it. We walk lakeshore yards in Burlington and Oakville before quoting and will tell you if a spot is going to cost you on hydro.

faq.q: Can I put a hot tub on a townhome terrace or condo balcony in Oakville or Mississauga?
faq.a: Sometimes. A Nordic Sport All-In-110V at $7,295 or a Jacuzzi J-215 is light enough for many rooftop terraces, but the structure has to be confirmed by the builder or an engineer and the condo board has to approve it in writing. Ground floor townhome patios are easier and usually take a J-315 or Aquasolus The Brook. Bring your floor plan and we will tell you what fits through the gate.

faq.q: My side yard in Milton is under four feet wide. How does a tub get to the back?
faq.a: Most tubs travel on their side on a spa dolly and need about 36 inches of clear width plus a straight shot, so we measure gate posts, air conditioner pads and downspouts before booking. If the path is too tight we book a crane and lift over the garage, which adds a few hundred dollars and takes about an hour. Either way we confirm the plan with you before delivery day.

faq.q: Do I need a permit or a setback approval for a hot tub in Burlington, Oakville or Milton?
faq.a: Each municipality treats hot tubs differently, and the rules on fencing, lockable covers and distance from the property line are not the same in Burlington as they are in Oakville, Milton or Hamilton. Check with your town before you pour a pad, and ask about the electrical permit at the same time. Your ESA licensed electrician files the electrical permit; we help with the drawings the town may ask for.

faq.q: We are on well water in Carlisle. Does that change how the tub is maintained?
faq.a: Yes. Halton and Flamborough wells tend to run hard with some iron, which stains acrylic and clouds the water if you fill straight from the hose. We fill through a pre-filter, balance calcium first and run a metal sequestrant on the initial fill. After that the Jacuzzi CLEARRAY system and normal weekly care keep it clear, and we test a sample of your well water in the showroom before you buy.

swim-spa.intro: Halton has two kinds of swim spa buyer: the lakeshore homeowner replacing an aging in-ground pool, and the new subdivision family who never had room for one. Both are swimming in January.
body: The pool-sized yards in Old Oakville, Roseland and Lorne Park are where most of our swim spas end up, often on the footprint of a pool that was costing more to open and close than it was worth. A Jacuzzi J-16 PowerPro or SwimLife SwimExpert AquaStream 17 fits inside the old shell area, and the existing electrical run to the pool pump is often reusable once an ESA licensed electrician sizes it. On a new lot in Milton or north Oakville the 14 foot models, the J-14 PowerActive at $41,395 and the SwimFit SwimStream 14 at $38,095, fit a rear yard that would never take a pool.

Who swims: triathletes training for open water season on Lake Ontario, masters swimmers who are tired of lane schedules, hockey and rowing families with teenagers, and people rehabbing knees and shoulders on their physiotherapist's advice. Serious swimmers pick the J-19 PowerPro at $58,995 for its current. Households that want both a workout and a soak choose the J-19DT PowerPro at $60,895 or the SwimExpert DualStream 19 at $56,095, each with a separate hot water zone. The J-13 PowerPlay at $33,195 is the family choice with eight seats and a gentler current the kids can play against.

Delivery is by crane in nearly every Halton yard, lifting over the house from the street, so we look at overhead wires, tree canopy and where the truck can sit before we quote. The town may require a road occupancy permit for the crane on a busy street, so check with them early. The spa sits on a reinforced concrete pad or is partly sunk into a deck; on Halton clay the pad design matters, and we supply the specification your contractor needs. A full-foam shell and a fitted cover keep it swimmable through a lakeshore winter without startling hydro bills.

faq.q: Can a swim spa go where my old in-ground pool used to be?
faq.a: Often, yes, and it is one of the most common jobs we do in Oakville and south Burlington. The old pool is demolished and backfilled with compacted granular, then a new pad is poured on top; the existing pool electrical is sometimes reusable after inspection. You keep the patio and the landscaping and lose the opening, closing and heating bills that came with the pool.

faq.q: How does a crane delivery work on a narrow lakeshore street?
faq.a: We visit first and plan where the crane and the flatbed will sit, which side of the house the lift clears and whether any hydro lines cross the path. On a tight street we may need a road occupancy permit, which the town issues, and we coordinate the time so neighbours are warned. The lift itself takes under an hour once the crane is set up.

faq.q: Which length is right for a triathlete versus a family?
faq.a: A serious swimmer wants the strongest current and the longest lane, which means a 19 foot PowerPro or the SwimExpert DualStream 19. A recreational swimmer who mostly wants to exercise is well served by a 14 or 16 foot model. Families who will spend more time playing than doing laps should look at the J-13 PowerPlay or J-12 Flow, which trade current strength for seats.

faq.q: Will I actually use a swim spa in January in Halton?
faq.a: Our customers do. The water sits at your chosen temperature under an insulated cover, so you open it, swim, and close it again; the air temperature matters less than you expect once you are moving. Lakeshore wind is the real factor, so we place the spa where the house or a fence blocks it. A short covered walkway from the door to the spa makes the difference between using it and admiring it.

faq.q: Do I need a fence around a swim spa?
faq.a: Most Halton municipalities treat a swim spa like a pool for enclosure purposes because of its depth, but the rules differ between Burlington, Oakville, Milton, Halton Hills and Hamilton. A lockable safety cover is sometimes accepted in place of a fence, sometimes not. Check with your town before you order so the fence or cover is part of the plan, not an afterthought.

sauna.intro: Halton became a sauna market before most of Ontario did, and this is the showroom where every Clearlight Sanctuary infrared cabin and both Serenity cedar outdoor saunas are heated and ready to sit in, beside the Chill Tubs cold plunges that finish the routine.
body: For a townhome in north Oakville, a Milton semi or a Mississauga condo, the Clearlight Sanctuary line answers where a sauna goes. The Sanctuary 1 at $10,495 fits a den or a home gym corner, plugs into any outlet and includes an AROMA ONE aromatherapy diffuser. The Sanctuary 2 at $11,795 is the one most Burlington townhome couples choose for an unfinished basement, and it is the cabin we most often deliver alongside a Chill Tubs Essential. The Sanctuary C at $14,495 is the corner cabin; the four seat Sanctuary Y at $13,995 suits a family. Measure the basement ceiling first: new builds clear it, some older Aldershot bungalows do not.

Out in Carlisle, Kilbride and rural Halton Hills the lot has room for a proper outdoor sauna, and we recommend Serenity cedar. The Serenity Mini at $14,995 suits a couple on a gravel pad or deck footings; the full size Serenity Sauna at $17,495 seats a family. Pricing is for knotty Western red cedar, clear grade is available, and the heater is sold separately. An electric heater needs a 240V circuit from an ESA licensed electrician, often a long trench; a wood-burning heater needs no hydro and suits a sauna down by a pond. Setbacks vary, so check with the city and, near Mount Nemo, the escarpment commission.

The routine that sells saunas here is contrast: heat, cold plunge, rest, repeat. Cyclists who train on the Milton hills and velodrome, hospital staff coming off nights and 403 commuters who need to sleep all buy the same setup: a sauna beside a Chill Tubs plunge. Indoors that is a Sanctuary cabin in the basement with an Essential Bath or Pod and a floor drain nearby. Outdoors it is a Serenity on the deck with an Obsidian or Pro beside it and a path you will walk barefoot in February. In winter the plunge holds temperature alone; in August the chiller earns its keep.

faq.q: Where does an infrared sauna go in a townhome with no spare room?
faq.a: Look at the garage, the unfinished side of the basement, a large walk-in closet or the corner of the main bedroom. The Sanctuary 1 needs roughly the footprint of a shower stall and the Sanctuary C is built for a corner, so two walls of a room are enough. Both run on a standard outlet, so no rewiring is needed, and the cabin comes apart if you move to a bigger house in Milton or Oakville later.

faq.q: Can a Serenity cedar sauna handle a Halton winter outdoors?
faq.a: Yes. It is built in Canada from Western red cedar for exactly this climate, and the roof carries the kind of snow Georgetown and Kilbride get on the escarpment. Cedar handles freeze and thaw cycles without rot, and the sauna is at its best on a January night when the steam meets the cold. Keep the door path shovelled and set the building on a level pad or footings so meltwater drains away from the base.

faq.q: Do I need a permit for an outdoor sauna on a rural lot in Carlisle or Kilbride?
faq.a: Probably, and the answer depends on where you are. Carlisle falls under the City of Hamilton, Kilbride under Burlington, and much of the land along the escarpment is also under Niagara Escarpment planning controls, so a small accessory building can need more than one approval. Ask the municipality about setbacks and permits before you order the pad, and tell them whether the heater is electric or wood-burning, since a chimney can change the requirements.

faq.q: How should I build a sauna and cold plunge routine at home?
faq.a: Start with the sauna for fifteen to twenty minutes, then one to three minutes in the plunge at about 5 to 10 degrees Celsius, then rest until you feel normal before the next round. Two or three rounds is plenty. Athletes tend to finish on cold; people using it for sleep usually finish on heat. Place the two within a few steps of each other so you actually make the transition in winter, and keep a towel and slippers by the door.

faq.q: Does a Chill Tubs cold plunge need plumbing if I put it beside my sauna?
faq.a: No fixed plumbing. The Chill Tub Essential fills from a garden hose or a bucket and drains with a hose, and its chiller plugs into a standard outlet. Indoors you want a floor drain or a laundry sink nearby for the occasional refill; outdoors a hose bib does the job. We can quote the Chill Tub together with any Sanctuary cabin and deliver and set up both on the same day.

hot-tub.small: The compact and 110V tubs here go to Aldershot bungalows with a small back patio, uptown Oakville townhomes with a ground floor terrace and downsizers moving into new builds off Appleby Line. The Jacuzzi J-315 and J-215 seat three and fit through a standard gate; the J-404L gives a couple a lounger in a four seat footprint. The Nordic Sport All-In-110V at $7,295 and Retreat All-In-110V at $9,195 plug into a dedicated outlet, which suits a condo terrace where a 240V run is not an option. Aquasolus The Brook at $10,995 includes White Glove delivery and setup.
hot-tub.medium: Five and six seat tubs are the sweet spot for the subdivision lots in Millcroft, the Orchard, Alton Village and south Milton, where the rear yard is wide but not deep. The Jacuzzi J-335 at $21,995 is our most popular tub in Burlington for exactly that reason. The J-375 and J-355 add power and a lounger, the J-445 and J-435 bring the J-400 waterfall and lighting to a lot that faces the neighbours, and the J-508L is the six seat version of the flagship. The Wellness Shop Ontario L S103 and S105 and Aquasolus The Eden are the value picks at this size.
hot-tub.large: Seven seats and up belong on the lakeshore estates of Oakville and Roseland, the escarpment properties around Kilbride and Mount Nemo, and the Carlisle acreages where a whole extended family shows up on Sunday. The Jacuzzi J-509 at $39,595 is the top of the range with 76 jets; the J-495 seats nine and the floor model is $31,395. The J-385 and J-365 are the seven seat J-300 tubs families choose when the budget matters, and the J-285 and J-245 do the same in the J-200 line. The Wellness Shop Ontario S106 and Aquasolus The Calma round out the big tubs under $18,000.

productNotes.swim-spa: Swim spas in Halton replace pools on lakeshore lots and stand in for pools on new ones. The Jacuzzi PowerPro line has the current that triathletes training for Lake Ontario want; PowerActive delivers most of it for less; PowerPlay and Flow are the family pools with eight seats. SwimLife SwimExpert and SwimFit carry the deepest discounts in the catalogue right now, and the DualStream 19 includes an attached five person hot tub with its own controls. Nearly every one is delivered by crane over the house, and we handle the pad specification for Halton clay.
productNotes.sauna: This showroom carries more sauna than any other Wellness Shop location because Halton asked for it. Clearlight Sanctuary infrared cabins from $10,495 go indoors, plug into an ordinary outlet and suit townhomes and condos from Mississauga to Milton; and the Sanctuary 2, 3 and Y are the ones most often paired with a Chill Tubs cold plunge. Serenity cedar outdoor saunas from $14,995 go on rural lots in Carlisle, Kilbride and Halton Hills with an electric or wood-burning heater sold separately. Every one of them is heated on our floor so you can sit in it before deciding.
productNotes.cold-plunge: Chill Tubs cold plunges are the second half of the routine for most Halton sauna buyers. The Essential Bath and Essential Pod are the compact starting points and sit naturally beside a Clearlight Sanctuary 2, 3 or Y; the Obsidian and the Pro are the full size chilled tubs for a deck beside a Serenity sauna or a basement gym. All four hold a set temperature year round with a built-in chiller, fill from a hose and need only a standard outlet. Pricing is showroom only, so ask when you visit or send the form.

financing: Most of our Halton customers have just closed on a house in Milton or Georgetown, are carrying an Oakville mortgage, or are Aldershot retirees keeping their capital invested, so financing is how most tubs and saunas leave this showroom. A Nordic Retreat All-In-110V works out to about $18.62 bi-weekly and a Retreat SE to about $19.38, and a sauna plus cold plunge package can be financed as a single plan so the whole routine goes in at once. Red Tag clearance pricing and financing can be used together, so the 20% comes off first and the payments are calculated on the reduced price. Apply in the showroom or through the form for terms.
showroom: You will find us at 3073 North Service Road in Burlington, right off the QEW at Guelph Line, with a full parking lot and no downtown traffic to fight. The floor holds the widest Jacuzzi selection in Halton, a full line of swim spas with water in them, every Clearlight Sanctuary cabin heated and ready, both Serenity cedar saunas assembled so you can step inside and smell the wood, and the Chill Tubs plunges running cold. Most people in Oakville, Aldershot, Waterdown and Milton are here in twenty minutes or less.

A good visit takes about an hour. Bring photos of the yard or the basement, a rough idea of the gate width and where the electrical panel sits, and a bathing suit if you want to wet test a Jacuzzi or try the sauna and plunge together. We will narrow the catalogue to three or four options that fit the space and the budget, price the delivery honestly, including any crane, and tell you which municipality to call about permits. Evenings and Saturdays are busiest with QEW commuters; weekday mornings are quiet if you want time.

Oakville.lead: Oakville is our largest market outside Burlington itself, from the lakeshore estates of Old Oakville and Morrison to the new streets north of Dundas where the lots are narrow and the basements are unfinished.
body: South of the QEW the housing is mature: deep lots in Old Oakville, Morrison, Bronte and Glen Abbey with pools that are reaching the end of their lives and trees that have grown over the side yard. This is where most of our swim spas and seven seat Jacuzzi tubs go, usually by crane over the garage. A J-19DT PowerPro or SwimExpert DualStream 19 on the footprint of a retired pool is a job we do several times a season, and the J-508 and J-509 suit households that entertain on the lake.

North of Dundas, in Joshua Creek, River Oaks and the newest phases along Trafalgar, the yards are tight and the gates are narrow, so the J-335, J-355 and Nordic Retreat SE are the tubs that fit, and Clearlight Sanctuary cabins go into basements that were roughed in for a gym. Staff from Oakville Trafalgar Memorial Hospital and Sheridan College are regulars for infrared saunas. Oakville is on municipal water, so water care is straightforward, and the town has its own rules on hot tub enclosures, so check with them before you set the pad.
Oakville.drive: Take the QEW west toward Hamilton, exit at Guelph Line and turn onto the North Service Road; the showroom is right there. From Bronte or Glen Abbey it is about fifteen minutes.

Milton.lead: Milton is where Halton's new subdivisions are, and every yard south of Derry Road seems to have the same four foot gate, the same rear lot line and the same unfinished basement waiting for a sauna.
body: The houses off Britannia, Louis St. Laurent and Derry are new enough that the electrical panel is in an open basement a few feet from the back wall, which makes the tub install one of the cheapest in our territory. The lots are narrow, so the J-335, J-325 and J-235 are common picks, and the Aquasolus The Eden and Wellness Shop Ontario L S103 win over families watching the budget after a big closing. A dolly delivery through the side gate is standard, and we measure the gate and the air conditioner clearance beforehand.

Milton also has the escarpment. Campbellville, Brookville and the country lots along the Sixth Line and Bell School Line have well water, room for a Serenity cedar sauna and a longer hydro run to think about. Cyclists who ride the escarpment climbs and train at the velodrome are the core of our sauna and cold plunge business here, and a Sanctuary 3 with a Chill Tubs Essential beside it is the usual first purchase. Milton has grown quickly, so ask the town about current hot tub and accessory building rules before you order.
Milton.drive: From Milton take Britannia Road west to Guelph Line, then follow Guelph Line south down the escarpment through Kilbride and Lowville to the QEW. Allow about half an hour.

Waterdown.lead: Waterdown sits on top of the escarpment above Aldershot, a village core with mature lots surrounded by a decade of new subdivisions, and it gets more snow and wind than the lakeshore below.
body: The new streets east of Highway 6 and north of Dundas are typical Halton and Hamilton new builds: narrow lots, tight gates, unfinished basements and young families. The J-335 and the Nordic Retreat SE are the tubs that fit the yard, and the Clearlight Sanctuary 2 is the basement sauna that fits the budget. Because Waterdown is on the escarpment plateau, expect more snow on the cover than a Burlington neighbour gets and plan the pad so cleared snow has somewhere to go that is not the cabinet.

The older village core along Mill Street and Dundas has larger lots, older wiring and sometimes a detached garage blocking the side yard, so a crane lift is more common than in the subdivisions. Beyond the village, Flamborough properties toward Carlisle run on wells and septic and have room for a Serenity Sauna with a wood-burning heater. Waterdown is part of the City of Hamilton, so its permit and setback rules are Hamilton's, not Burlington's; check with them before you pour anything.
Waterdown.drive: Take Waterdown Road south down the escarpment to Highway 403, merge east onto the QEW and exit at Guelph Line to the North Service Road. About fifteen minutes door to door.

Aldershot.lead: Aldershot is the west end of Burlington along Plains Road, a mix of postwar bungalows on deep lots, newer infill near the GO station and the quiet streets backing onto the Royal Botanical Gardens.
body: The bungalows off Plains Road and Waterdown Road have generous rear yards and a side yard that often runs beside a carport, so a dolly delivery usually works and the panel in the basement is a short run to the back. Retirees and downsizers here choose two to four seat tubs, the J-315, J-404L and Aquasolus The Brook, and the smaller Clearlight cabins, though basement ceiling height in a 1950s bungalow can rule out the taller Sanctuary models, so measure first.

Newer townhomes and mid-rise buildings near Aldershot GO bring a different question: what fits on a terrace and what the board allows. A Nordic Sport All-In-110V or a Sanctuary 1 in a den is usually the answer. Lakeshore streets near LaSalle Park face the same wind off Hamilton Harbour that the rest of the Burlington waterfront gets, so tub placement out of the west wind matters. Aldershot is Burlington, so it follows the city's rules and municipal water.
Aldershot.drive: Follow Plains Road east to Brant Street, then north to the North Service Road and east to Guelph Line, or take the 403 east onto the QEW and exit at Guelph Line. Ten minutes.

Halton Hills.lead: Halton Hills is the rural north of the region, Acton, Glen Williams, Limehouse and the farm and estate lots between them, where properties are measured in acres and hydro runs are measured in hundreds of feet.
body: Country properties here have what the lakeshore does not: room. A Serenity Sauna at $17,495 with a wood-burning heater can sit down by the pond or at the tree line without a trench for hydro, and a full size Jacuzzi J-485 or J-475 on a deck off the kitchen is a straightforward delivery because the truck can drive right up to it. The variable is the panel. Older farmhouses may have 100 amp service already spoken for by a barn or a shop, so an ESA licensed electrician should do a load calculation before you decide between a 240V Jacuzzi and a Nordic Retreat All-In-110V.

Nearly everyone outside Acton and Georgetown is on a well and septic, so we set up water care for hard water and plan the drain so a tub change does not overload the septic bed. Winters up here are colder and snowier than Burlington's, with drifting on open fields, so a tight cover and a cover lifter are not optional. Acton itself has older in-town lots with narrow side yards, closer to the Aldershot pattern than the farm one. Halton Hills has its own accessory building and setback rules; ask the town.
Halton Hills.drive: From Acton take Highway 25 south to the 401, or from Glen Williams take Trafalgar Road south, then the 401 west to Guelph Line and Guelph Line south to the QEW. Roughly 50 minutes.

Georgetown.lead: Georgetown is the largest town in Halton Hills, an older main street on the Credit River surrounded by subdivisions from every decade since the sixties and served by its own GO station on the Kitchener line.
body: The housing here spans older streets near downtown and the Credit with deep lots and detached garages, the sixties and seventies subdivisions of Delrex with wide lots and side yards a dolly can use, and the newer south Georgetown streets with narrow lots and a four foot gate. That range means we sell everything from a J-509 for a big family in an older house to a J-325 for a narrow new build. Basements in the older stock are often finished, so the panel run needs a plan before the electrician arrives.

Commuters on the Kitchener GO line and people who drive the 401 to Mississauga are the main buyers, and after a long day they want a tub that is hot when they get home, so the Jacuzzi models with the SmartTub app are popular here. Georgetown sits higher than the lakeshore and gets real snow, so we recommend a cover lifter and a pad placement that keeps the shovelled snow off the cabinet. Glen Williams and the rural fringe are on wells; the town itself is on municipal water.
Georgetown.drive: Take Trafalgar Road south to Highway 401, head west to the Guelph Line exit at Campbellville, then follow Guelph Line south down the escarpment to the QEW. About 45 minutes.

Mississauga.lead: Mississauga's west and south end, Clarkson, Lorne Park, Port Credit, Erin Mills and Streetsville, is a short QEW run from our floor, and the city's condo and townhome market is our biggest source of infrared sauna buyers.
body: Lorne Park and Clarkson have the same pattern as Old Oakville: big treed lots, aging pools and detached garages that mean crane deliveries. Swim spas replacing pools, seven seat J-500 tubs and Serenity cedar saunas on a large lakeshore deck all sell well here. Erin Mills, Meadowvale and Streetsville are established subdivisions with reasonable side yards and a finished basement, so a dolly delivery and a longer electrical run are typical, and the J-375, J-445 and Wellness Shop Ontario S104 are common choices for families.

The condo towers around Square One and the townhome complexes across the city are a different customer. A Clearlight Sanctuary 1 or 2 fits a den or a second bedroom, plugs into the wall and needs no board approval beyond what any appliance does, which is why so many of them go to Mississauga. Terrace hot tubs are possible on some buildings with a Nordic 110V model, but only after the board and an engineer sign off. Mississauga is on municipal water and has its own permit rules, so check with the city.
Mississauga.drive: Take the QEW west past Oakville, exit at Guelph Line in Burlington and turn onto the North Service Road. From Clarkson it is about twenty minutes; from Square One allow thirty-five outside rush hour.

Carlisle.lead: Carlisle is a rural village in Flamborough, technically the City of Hamilton, with horse farms, acreages and a village core on Centre Road, and it is the heart of our Serenity outdoor sauna business.
body: Carlisle properties have room to put a sauna where it belongs: down by the pond, at the edge of the paddock or on a deck that looks out over the fields. The Serenity Sauna at $17,495 in knotty cedar with a wood-burning heater is the usual choice because it needs no hydro at that distance, and a Chill Tub Pro beside it completes the setup. Hot tub buyers here go big, a J-495 or J-485 on a deck off the kitchen, because the extended family arrives on weekends and the truck can drive straight to the spot.

Everything in Carlisle runs on a well and a septic system. Flamborough well water is hard and often carries iron, so we fill through a pre-filter and set up water care accordingly, and we plan drain-downs so they do not hit the septic bed all at once. Winters are colder and windier than Burlington's with open fields to the west, so a sturdy cover and a windbreak matter. Carlisle follows Hamilton's permit and setback rules for accessory buildings and hot tubs, so check with the city rather than with Burlington.
Carlisle.drive: Take Centre Road south to Highway 5, head east into Burlington, then Guelph Line south to the QEW and the North Service Road. Allow about 25 minutes.

Kilbride.lead: Kilbride is the hamlet in rural north Burlington on the escarpment, between Mount Nemo and Lowville, where estate lots and old farmhouses share the ridge and the view runs all the way to the lake.
body: Escarpment lots are the most beautiful and the most complicated sites we work on. Many are sloped, so a sauna or tub needs a level pad or a built-up deck, and the access route for a crane or a truck has to be walked in advance. A Serenity Mini at $14,995 fits a couple on a deck facing the view; the full Serenity Sauna suits the larger properties along Cedar Springs Road. Kilbride is on wells, so water care is set up for hard water, and the hydro panel in an older farmhouse may need an upgrade before a 240V Jacuzzi goes in.

Snow and ice are heavier up here than in the city below, and the wind across the ridge is real, so cover quality and placement out of the west wind are the first things we discuss. Much of Kilbride falls under Niagara Escarpment planning controls as well as Burlington's own rules, so a shed-sized sauna can need a development permit that a downtown Burlington homeowner never thinks about. Ask the city and the escarpment commission early. The people who live here tend to want the outdoor sauna and cold plunge routine more than a tub, and the setting suits it.
Kilbride.drive: Take Kilbride Street or Cedar Springs Road to Guelph Line and follow it straight south through Lowville and down the escarpment to the QEW; the showroom is at the interchange. About twenty minutes.

productBlurbs.j-509: Eight open seats and 76 jets make this the tub for the Lakeshore Road households in south Oakville that host the whole family on Sunday. It is the widest Jacuzzi we carry, so we plan the crane lift over the garage before quoting on the older treed lots. True Water care with ProClarity 6-Stage filtration keeps a tub this busy clear between weekly checks. At $39,595 on Red Tag pricing it is the top of the range, and it sells to people who know exactly why.
productBlurbs.j-508: Families in Glen Abbey with two teenagers and their friends land on the J-508 more than any other J-500 tub. Seven open seats mean nobody argues over a lounger, and 56 jets with the J-500 waterfall and lighting turn a Friday night into something the kids stay home for. It shares True Water care and ProClarity 6-Stage filtration with the larger J-509, in a footprint that still fits a Millcroft rear yard with a dolly delivery down the side yard rather than over the roof.
productBlurbs.j-508l: Choose the J-508L when two people in the household want to lie back and the rest are happy sitting up. Six seats and 60 jets in the flagship shell suit the couples on Roseland's deep lots who soak most nights and entertain a few times a year. The J-500 cabinet looks right beside the stone and glass of a renovated lakeshore house, which matters more here than it does inland. Same $35,695 sale price as the seven seat J-508, so the decision is purely about layout.
productBlurbs.j-408: Waterdown's newer streets above the escarpment get a longer winter than the lakeshore below, and the J-408 is built for it: full foam insulation under seven open seats, True Water care and ProClarity 5-Stage filtration, at $29,995 on Red Tag pricing. The open layout means a hockey team's worth of kids fit after practice at Harry Howell Arena, and the J4 cabinet holds up to the freeze and thaw on the plateau. Plan the pad so shovelled snow lands away from the cabinet.
productBlurbs.j-408l: Executives who sit on the 403 from Ancaster or the QEW from Mississauga want a lounger waiting when they get home, and the J-408L is the one we point them to. The lounge seat runs a full leg and back massage from 39 jets, five upright seats take the rest of the family, and the SmartTub app has it at temperature before the garage door opens. Against the open seating J-408 at the same price you trade one seat for the lounger, and most commuters make that trade.
productBlurbs.j-404l: Downsizers moving from a big Tyandaga house into a bungalow or a new build near Appleby GO rarely need seven seats, and the J-404L gives a couple the lounger and the J4 build in a four seat shell that fits a small patio. Thirty-two jets is plenty for two people who use it every night, and the smaller water volume heats faster and costs less to hold through a February on the lake. At $25,195 with Red Tag pricing it is the premium small tub on our floor.
productBlurbs.j-495: Nine seats is a lot of hot tub, and the J-495 goes to the Carlisle acreages and Cedar Springs Road properties where the extended family arrives on weekends and the truck can drive right to the deck. Seventy-one jets keep every seat working, and the open layout means grandparents and teenagers share it without anyone climbing over a lounger. Our 2025 floor model is $31,395, and because Carlisle runs on wells we set True Water care up for hard water before the first fill.
productBlurbs.j-485: Seven open seats and 49 jets in the J-400 shell make the J-485 the family tub for the wide seventies lots of Delrex in Georgetown, where a dolly delivery down the side yard is easy and a big deck off the kitchen is already waiting. Kids coming off the ice at Gellert can pile in without a seating plan. The 2025 floor model at $26,295 is the strongest value in our seven seat range this season, with the same True Water care and ProClarity 5-Stage filtration as the new stock.
productBlurbs.j-475: Nurses and paramedics coming off nights at Joseph Brant buy the J-475 for the lounger, not the party. Fifty-five jets are concentrated where a sore back and tired legs want them, and the six upright seats still take the family on the weekend. It is the lounge version of the J-485 at the same price, and our 2025 floor model is $26,295 with the full warranty. Full foam insulation and a fitted cover keep the standby cost sensible on an Elizabeth Gardens lot that catches the lake wind.
productBlurbs.j-445: On the new streets of Alton Village the gate is under four feet and the panel is in an open basement near the back wall, which makes the J-445 one of the simplest installs we do: a dolly delivery, a short electrical run and six open seats with 45 jets ready the same week. The waterfall and lighting give a yard that faces the neighbours something to look at after dark. The 2025 floor model at $23,995 gets a young family into a J-400 series Jacuzzi for J-300 money.
productBlurbs.j-435: A finished basement in Erin Mills means the electrician runs conduit around the outside of the house instead of through the ceiling, and the J-435 is worth that extra run: a lounger with 47 jets for the two adults, five seats for everyone else, and a J-400 cabinet that looks finished from the kitchen window. It is the lounge counterpart to the open seating J-445, and the 2025 floor model at $24,995 is the lowest price on our floor for a J-400 lounger.
productBlurbs.j-385: Streetsville families who want seven seats without a J-500 budget pick the J-385, the top of the J-300 range with 51 jets and an open layout that takes the whole hockey car pool. CLEARRAY Active Oxygen water care and the ProClear skimming weir mean less time on chemistry for parents who already have enough on the calendar. At $26,595 on Red Tag pricing it sits well below the seven seat J-400 tubs, and it still goes through most Streetsville side yards on a dolly.
productBlurbs.j-365: Headon Forest and Brant Hills have the sixties and seventies lots where three generations still gather, and the J-365 seats seven of them for $24,795 on Red Tag pricing. Forty-six jets are spread across open seating so a grandparent gets the same massage as a teenager, and CLEARRAY Active Oxygen keeps the water clear through a busy March Break. Against the J-345 it adds five jets for a modest step in price, and most Burlington families make that step.
productBlurbs.j-345: A first hot tub after a big Milton closing is a common story on our floor, and the J-345 is where it usually ends: seven seats, 41 jets and the full Jacuzzi build for $23,195 on Red Tag pricing. The lots off Louis St. Laurent are narrow but the basements are open, so delivery and electrical are among the cheapest in our territory. CLEARRAY Active Oxygen and the ProClear weir keep water care simple for a household learning the routine for the first time.
productBlurbs.j-375: Cyclists who ride the Rattlesnake Point and Sixth Line climbs come home wanting a lounger, and the J-375 has the strongest one in the J-300 range with 52 jets working the legs and lower back. Five upright seats mean the rest of the household still gets a soak. Full foam insulation keeps it cheap to hold at temperature on an exposed hillside lot, and at $25,295 on Red Tag pricing it is the lounger we recommend to anyone who trains hard and sleeps badly.
productBlurbs.j-355: Shoreacres couples who soak most nights and have the neighbours over a few times a summer get the balance right with the J-355: a lounger with 44 jets for the two of you, five more seats when the deck fills up. The cabinet and cover hinge can be turned out of the lake wind that runs up Shoreacres Creek, which we plan on the site visit. At $24,795 on Red Tag pricing it is a small step past the J-335 in price and jets.
productBlurbs.j-335: More J-335 tubs go into the Orchard than any other model we sell, and the reason is simple: six seats with a lounger and 42 jets in a shell that clears a standard gate on a dolly and sits on a pad the size of a parking space. At $21,995 on Red Tag pricing it is the entry point to the J-300 line, with CLEARRAY Active Oxygen and full foam insulation that keep both chemicals and hydro modest. Ask for a wet test; most people decide in the lounger.
productBlurbs.j-325: Churchill Meadows townhomes with a ground floor patio and a rear lane are exactly the lots the J-325 was built for: five open seats, 23 jets and a compact footprint that leaves room for a table. It is the least expensive open seating tub in the J-300 line at $20,495 on Red Tag pricing, and fewer jets suits people who want a warm soak more than a massage. Check with your condo corporation on the pad before you order; we can supply the drawings.
productBlurbs.j-315: Two people, a lounger and a patio the size of a parking pad near Bronte Harbour: that is the J-315 customer. Three seats and 23 jets in the smallest J-300 shell heat quickly, sip hydro and still carry CLEARRAY Active Oxygen water care, and the lounger is a proper full length seat rather than a compromise. At $18,795 on Red Tag pricing it is the cheapest way into the J-300 line, and it rides a dolly on its side to the back of a small lot.
productBlurbs.j-285: Halton families who sold the Muskoka cottage and want the Friday night feeling in the backyard put the money into a J-285: seven open seats, 42 jets and Jacuzzi build quality at $18,695 on Red Tag pricing. CLEARRAY UV-C water care and the ProClassic filter with a ProCatch bag are simple enough that a teenager can run the weekly check. It is the largest J-200 tub and it goes to the wide lots in Mountainside and Palmer where a big deck already exists.
productBlurbs.j-245: Acton households with a big yard and a modest budget get seven seats for $16,295 on Red Tag pricing with the J-245, the most affordable seven seat Jacuzzi we sell. Thirty-seven jets across open seating suit a family that soaks together more than it massages, and the ProClassic filtration with a ProCatch bag copes with the leaves that come with an older Acton lot. Well water is common north of Georgetown, so we pre-filter the first fill and balance calcium before the CLEARRAY UV-C system takes over.
productBlurbs.j-275: Clearance is the whole story on the J-275: a six seat Jacuzzi lounger with 38 jets and CLEARRAY UV-C water care, from $14,695 on 2025 floor and flash stock while it lasts. That price puts a Jacuzzi lounger within reach of first time buyers in Milton's newer phases and in the townhomes near Burlington GO who assumed they were shopping Nordic or Aquasolus. Quantities are what is on the floor, so if you want one, come in this week rather than next month.
productBlurbs.j-235: Shift workers at the Ford plant in Oakville and at Oakville Trafalgar Memorial want a lounger that is hot at seven in the morning, and the J-235 delivers it without a J-300 budget: six seats, a 34 jet lounger and CLEARRAY UV-C water care for $16,295 on Red Tag pricing. The smaller shell heats quickly after a cover-off session and fits the narrow lots around Kerr Village. It is the lounge version of the J-245, trading one seat for a place to lie down.
productBlurbs.j-225: Port Credit lots are short, and the J-225 is the Jacuzzi that fits them: five open seats and 26 jets in a footprint that leaves the rest of the patio usable, at $14,695 on Red Tag pricing. Open seating means five adults sit comfortably, which is more than most tubs this size manage. CLEARRAY UV-C keeps the chemistry simple, and the lighter shell rides a dolly to the back, which matters on a street where a crane cannot park.
productBlurbs.j-215: For two people who will use it every single night, the J-215 is the least expensive Jacuzzi lounger on our floor at $14,095 on Red Tag pricing. Three seats with 21 jets, a full length lounger and CLEARRAY UV-C water care in a shell small enough to sit on a Longmoor bungalow patio without swallowing it. The low water volume is the point: it heats fast, it costs little to hold at temperature through January, and it drains and refills in an afternoon.
productBlurbs.retreat-all-in-110v: When the panel in an older Limehouse farmhouse is already spoken for by the barn, the Nordic Retreat All-In-110V solves it: plug the included GFCI cord into a dedicated 15 amp outlet and five people are soaking that evening, with no 240V trench across the yard. Thirteen jets and a round open layout make it a social tub rather than a massage chair. At $9,195 it finances from about $18.62 bi-weekly OAC, and the Nordic Clean ozone system keeps well water manageable.
productBlurbs.sport-all-in-110v: Rooftop terraces on the new townhome blocks along Dundas in north Burlington can take the Nordic Sport All-In-110V where a 240V tub is out of the question: it holds far less water than a full size tub, plugs into a standard outlet with the included GFCI cord, and needs no electrician. Fifteen jets around five seats give a couple and their guests a real soak. At $7,295 it is the least expensive hot tub on this site. Confirm the structure and the board first.
productBlurbs.retreat-se: Step up from the plug-and-play Nordics and the Retreat SE gives you 29 jets and a 220V 40 amp supply on the same five seat round shell, which is why it beats the Retreat All-In-110V for anyone who wants a massage rather than a warm soak. Meadowvale families on a subdivision lot with the panel a short run from the back wall find the 240V run short and cheap. At $10,195, roughly $19.38 bi-weekly OAC, it is Michigan-built, simple to service and small enough for a dolly delivery.
productBlurbs.ontario-s106: Two 6 HP pumps pushing 59 jets across seven open seats, built in the USA with Thermal Shield insulation, for $17,695: the Ontario S106 is the tub we show people who came in for a J-385 and blinked at the price. Families in West Oak Trails carrying a new Oakville mortgage take it home for the same reason. Ozone filtration with a 50 square foot flow-through filter keeps maintenance simple, and it sits on the floor beside the Jacuzzi range so you can try both.
productBlurbs.ontario-s104: Seven seats for $15,595 with two 6 HP pumps behind 54 jets makes the Ontario S104 the value seven seater in our own line, and it goes to Freelton and Flamborough properties where the truck drives right to the deck and the budget went into the house. Thermal Shield insulation is the difference on an open rural lot with wind across the fields in January. Ozone filtration copes with Flamborough well water after a pre-filtered first fill. It gives up five jets and the larger filter to the S106.
productBlurbs.ontario-l-s103: A six seat layout with a lounger, 51 jets and two 6 HP pumps for $15,595 is why the Ontario L S103 goes home with so many Waterdown families whose new build came with a narrow lot and a mortgage to match. Thermal Shield insulation earns its keep on the escarpment plateau where the cover carries more snow than a lakeshore tub ever sees. The lounger is full length, the remaining seats are upright, and the USA-built shell rides a dolly through a four foot gate.
productBlurbs.ontario-l-s105: Take the L S103 layout, add five jets and the GECKO K1000 keypad, and you have the Ontario L S105 at $17,695: six seats, a lounger, two 6 HP pumps and the easiest control panel in our own line to read at night. Tyandaga couples who want a powerful lounger without the Jacuzzi price are the usual buyers, and the Thermal Shield insulation keeps a tub on a ravine lot above the 403 affordable to run. Built in the USA, on our floor, ready for a wet test.
productBlurbs.the-brook: A first house in Georgetown South with a small patio and no appetite for a big tub is where Aquasolus The Brook lands: four open seats, 23 jets, a European-built shell from Superior Wellness and an ozone system, for $10,995 with White Glove delivery and setup already in the price. It costs less than any Jacuzzi on this site and still gives a couple a proper soak with room for two guests. Bring photos of the yard; it usually fits.
productBlurbs.the-cove: Seven seats for $11,995 is the headline on Aquasolus The Cove, and it is the tub for a Campbellville property where the yard is big, the family is bigger and the money went into the barn. Twenty-seven jets across open seating make it a soaking tub more than a massage tub, which suits a household that gathers in it rather than one person chasing a sore back. European-built by Superior Wellness with an ozone system, and White Glove delivery and setup are part of the price, not a surcharge.
productBlurbs.the-calma: Step up from The Cove to Aquasolus The Calma and you keep the seven open seats but gain ten jets and the NaturaBalance shell, at $13,995 including White Glove delivery and setup. Clarkson households replacing a worn out tub on an existing pad choose it because the ozone system and the European build from Superior Wellness feel a class above the price. It is the model we suggest to families who want everyone in the water together and have a budget that stops short of Jacuzzi.
productBlurbs.the-eden: Aquasolus The Eden is the lounger for people who commute from Aldershot GO and want to lie down when they get home, without spending Jacuzzi money: six seats, 42 jets, a full lounger and an ozone system at $13,995. White Glove delivery and setup are included, which matters on the older Aldershot streets where a carport narrows the side yard. It shares the NaturaBalance series with The Calma; choose this one if the lounger matters more than the seventh seat.
productBlurbs.j-19dt-powerpro: Nineteen feet of swim lane at one temperature and a separate hot tub zone at another is why the J-19DT PowerPro replaces an in-ground pool in Lorne Park. A triathlete trains against the PowerPro current in the morning and the family soaks in the hot end that night, 53 jets between them. It needs two circuits, a 20 amp and a 40 amp, and a crane lift over the house, both planned on the site visit. At $60,895 it is the top of our swim spa range.
productBlurbs.j-19-powerpro: The J-19 PowerPro is the single temperature lane for people who swim seriously: masters swimmers tired of booking lanes at Centennial Pool and open water racers who want to be ready for Lake Ontario in June. Nineteen feet, the PowerPro current that triathletes ask for, and four seats with 34 jets for the cool down. One 40 amp circuit and CLEARRAY Active Oxygen with dual 50 square foot filtration keep it simple. At $58,995 it trades the J-19DT's hot tub zone for a lower price and one long lane.
productBlurbs.j-16-powerpro: Sixteen feet is the length that fits inside the footprint of a retired pool on a Roseland lot without eating the whole patio, and the J-16 PowerPro brings the same current and 34 jets as the J-19 PowerPro to that shorter lane. Four seats give the family a place to soak after the swimmer is done. It runs on one 40 amp circuit, often reusing the old pool feed once an ESA licensed electrician inspects it, and at $54,295 it saves real money against the 19 foot version.
productBlurbs.j-14-powerpro: Fourteen feet with 51 jets and five seats is the PowerPro for a Palermo lot that is wide but not deep, where a 19 foot spa would touch both fences. The current is full PowerPro strength on a shorter lane, so a real swimmer still gets a workout, and the extra seats make it the hot tub too. One 40 amp circuit, CLEARRAY Active Oxygen water care, and delivery is planned on the site visit. At $48,795 it is the most affordable way into the PowerPro line.
productBlurbs.j-19dt-poweractive: Two temperatures, one crane lift: the J-19DT PowerActive gives a Glen Williams family the 19 foot swim zone and a separate hot tub zone for $53,295, with 51 jets split between them and six seats in total. The PowerActive current is gentler than PowerPro, which suits swimmers who train for fitness rather than a start line, and it needs the same 20 amp plus 40 amp pair of circuits. Four 50 square foot filters with CLEARRAY Active Oxygen keep two bodies of water clear with one weekly routine.
productBlurbs.j-19-poweractive: People rehabbing a knee or a shoulder on their physiotherapist's advice want a long, steady lane rather than a racing current, and the J-19 PowerActive gives them 19 feet of it for $51,395. Four seats with 32 jets handle the soak afterward, CLEARRAY Active Oxygen with dual 50 square foot filtration keeps the water clean, and one 40 amp circuit runs the lot. On a Lowville property with room to spare, it often comes straight off the flatbed onto the pad.
productBlurbs.j-16-poweractive: Bronte homeowners who want to swim through January without a pool heater bill get the J-16 PowerActive: a 16 foot lane under an insulated cover, four seats with 32 jets, and CLEARRAY Active Oxygen water care that holds up between weekly checks. The PowerActive current is enough for fitness swimming and aqua jogging without the PowerPro price, and at $46,495 it undercuts the J-16 PowerPro by a useful margin. One 40 amp circuit; a crane lift is standard on the mature lakeshore streets.
productBlurbs.j-14-poweractive: Joshua Creek lots were never going to take a pool, and the J-14 PowerActive is the swim spa that fits them: 14 feet, five seats and 49 jets, with a crane lift over the house from the street. The current handles lap swimming and resistance work, and with more seats than the longer PowerActive models it doubles as the family hot tub on weekends. At $41,395 on one 40 amp circuit with CLEARRAY Active Oxygen, it is the least expensive PowerActive we sell.
productBlurbs.j-13-powerplay: Eight seats and 38 jets in 13 feet make the J-13 PowerPlay the family pool for a Clearview household with three kids who will play against the current far more than they will do laps. The single 32 amp circuit is lighter than the PowerPro models need, so the electrical estimate is smaller, and the shorter length often lets us deliver through a wide side yard instead of over the roof. At $33,195 it costs less than a couple of our seven seat hot tubs and does twice the job.
productBlurbs.j-12-flow: Twelve feet, eight seats and a $30,695 price make the J-12 Flow the entry to swim spas for a Dynes family that wants the kids swimming in the yard and the adults soaking after. The current is built for play and gentle exercise rather than race training, and 31 jets do the hot tub work. CLEARRAY UV-C water care keeps it simple, and the 32 amp circuit is the smallest in our swim spa range. Against the J-13 PowerPlay you give up one foot and seven jets.
productBlurbs.swimexpert-dualstream-19: Down to $56,095 from $74,995, the SwimExpert DualStream 19 carries the deepest discount in our swim spa range, and it is the one Morrison households replacing a pool ask for by name. A 19 foot swim zone on one side, an attached five person hot tub with 30 jets and its own controls on the other, 53 jets in the swim end and a 20 amp plus 40 amp electrical pair. ClearStream mineral water care means less chlorine smell on a deck close to the neighbours.
productBlurbs.swimexpert-aquastream-17: Seventeen feet is the SwimExpert length for a Kilbride lot where a level pad has to be cut into the slope and every foot of spa is a foot more excavation. Three seats and 30 jets cover the cool down, one 40 amp circuit runs it, and the ClearStream mineral system is forgiving of the hard well water up on the escarpment. At $50,095 the AquaStream 17 is the middle length in the SwimExpert line, and the one most single swimmers choose.
productBlurbs.swimexpert-swimstream-14: Fourteen feet on a 32 amp circuit is the SwimExpert SwimStream 14, and it goes to the newer lots around Beaty where the yard is a rectangle behind a four foot gate and the panel is close to the back wall. Three seats, 30 jets and the SwimExpert swim system in the shortest lane SwimLife builds. ClearStream mineral water care suits a family that would rather swim than test water. At $44,795 it is the way into the SwimExpert line for less than most PowerActive models.
productBlurbs.swimfit-aquastream-17: SwimFit is the SwimLife line that skips the extras, and the AquaStream 17 shows how much that saves: 17 feet, three seats, 28 jets and ClearStream mineral water care for $43,795. On a Carlisle property where the flatbed can drive to the pad, delivery is simpler too. Against the SwimExpert AquaStream 17 you give up two jets for a meaningful drop in price, which is why it is the 17 footer we sell most to first time swim spa buyers.
productBlurbs.swimfit-swimstream-14: At $38,095 the SwimFit SwimStream 14 is the least expensive swim spa on this site, and it turns a narrow new lot off Appleby Line into a place to swim year round. Fourteen feet with three seats and 28 jets, on a 32 amp circuit that keeps the electrical quote small. ClearStream mineral water care means a softer feel and fewer chemicals for a household that just wants to get in. Fitness swimmers are well served; anyone training for open water should look at a longer lane.
productBlurbs.sanctuary-1: One person, twenty minutes, every morning before the QEW: that is the Sanctuary 1. It is the full spectrum infrared cabin that fits a den or a spare corner in a Mississauga condo, plugs into an ordinary outlet and comes with the AROMA ONE aromatherapy diffuser at no charge. True Wave heaters in a Basswood or Mahogany cabin, with Clearlight's lifetime warranty on both. At $10,495 it is the least expensive sauna we sell, and it is heated on our floor so you can sit in it before you decide.
productBlurbs.sanctuary-2: Couples in River Oaks who finished the lower level with a gym corner in mind end up with the Sanctuary 2 more than any other cabin: two seats, full spectrum infrared from True Wave heaters, a standard household circuit and a footprint that leaves room for the treadmill. Choose Basswood or Mahogany to match the room. At $11,795 it is the step most people take from the single seat cabin, and the lifetime warranty on cabin and heaters makes it a one time purchase. Measure the ceiling before you order.
productBlurbs.sanctuary-3: Three seats is where a sauna stops being personal and becomes the family's, and the Sanctuary 3 at $12,995 is the cabin for parents who spend winter evenings in the stands at Appleby Ice Centre and want to warm up properly afterwards. Full spectrum infrared from True Wave heaters, Basswood or Mahogany, and Clearlight's lifetime warranty on the cabin and heaters. Put a Chill Tub Essential nearby and you have the contrast routine the cyclists and hockey players in the house will actually use.
productBlurbs.sanctuary-5: Five seats instead of three is what the Sanctuary 5 adds over the Sanctuary 3, and at $13,995 it is the one trail runners and Bruce Trail regulars from Mount Nemo pick when the whole group wants in after a long day on the escarpment. Full spectrum infrared, True Wave heaters, Basswood or Mahogany, lifetime warranty on the cabin and the heaters. Bring the room dimensions and we will tell you whether it fits down the basement stairs of a Halton Hills farmhouse.
productBlurbs.sanctuary-y: The Sanctuary Y seats four at $13,995, the same price as the five seat Sanctuary 5, so families choose on footprint and layout rather than price: two parents and two teenagers in a Waterdown new build with an unfinished basement and long winters on the plateau. Full spectrum infrared from True Wave heaters, Basswood or Mahogany, and Clearlight's lifetime warranty on cabin and heaters. It is the cabin we most often see paired with a cold plunge in a household where everyone plays a different sport.
productBlurbs.sanctuary-c: Corner cabins solve the rec room that is already full, and the Sanctuary C is built to sit diagonally in the corner of a Pinedale rec room where a rectangular sauna would block the door. Four seats, full spectrum infrared from True Wave heaters, Basswood or Mahogany, and the lifetime warranty on cabin and heaters that comes with every Clearlight. At $14,495 it costs a little more than the Sanctuary Y for the same four seats; the corner footprint is what you are paying for.
productBlurbs.sanctuary-retreat: Top of the Clearlight line at $15,295, the Sanctuary Retreat is the four seat cabin for a Milton household that wants the lower level to feel like the spa they used to drive to. Full spectrum infrared from True Wave heaters, Basswood or Mahogany, and a lifetime warranty on the cabin and the heaters. Compared with the Sanctuary Y it is the flagship four seat room, and it is the cabin people book a second visit to sit in before they commit. Bring the stair and ceiling measurements.
productBlurbs.serenity-mini: Two people, a deck and a Millgrove winter: the Serenity Mini is the Canadian-made cedar sauna for the couple who want the outdoor experience without a building the size of a shed. Knotty Western red cedar at $14,995, clear cedar available, open bench seating and up to 194 degrees once you add the heater, which is sold separately as electric or wood-burning. On a village lot an electric heater on a 240V circuit is usual; on acreage the wood-burning option saves a trench.
productBlurbs.serenity-sauna: Full size and family sized, the Serenity Sauna at $17,495 in knotty cedar is the outdoor sauna for a Halton Hills acreage where the whole household goes out together on a Saturday night. Built in Canada from Western red cedar, open bench seating, up to 194 degrees with steam once the heater is in, and the heater is sold separately so you can choose electric or wood-burning based on how far the hydro is. Against the Serenity Mini you gain the room for the whole family at once.
productBlurbs.chill-tub-essential-bath: Compact enough for a Millcroft basement where the sauna is already in the corner and the laundry sink is a few steps away for refills, the Chill Tub Essential Bath is the starting point in the Chill Tubs line. It fills from a hose, holds a set cold temperature with its own chiller and plugs into a standard outlet, with no plumber involved. The sit-in shape suits one to three minutes between rounds of heat. Pricing is at the showroom, where it runs cold beside the Sanctuary cabins.
productBlurbs.chill-tub-essential-pod: Upright and round, the Chill Tub Essential Pod takes less floor than the Essential Bath and is the plunge for a downtown Burlington condo terrace near Spencer Smith Park where the sauna is a Sanctuary 1 inside and the routine is heat, cold, repeat. Fill it from a hose, plug the chiller into a standard outlet and it holds temperature through August without a bag of ice. Ask for pricing at the showroom; we keep one cold on the floor so you can test how long you last.
productBlurbs.chill-tub-obsidian: Full size and finished in black, the Chill Tub Obsidian is the outdoor plunge that sits on a Brookville deck beside a Serenity cedar sauna and looks like it belongs there. Its built-in chiller holds the water at your chosen temperature through a humid July, and in January the escarpment does most of the work on its own. Fill from a garden hose, plug into a standard outlet, drain with a hose. Pricing is at the showroom, and you can see it beside both Serenity saunas on our floor.
productBlurbs.chill-tub-pro: Built for the athlete rather than the hobbyist, the Chill Tub Pro is the plunge that Around the Bay runners and masters cyclists from across Halton ask for by name: the top of the four Chill Tubs models, sized for daily use. It works beside a Serenity sauna on a deck or a Sanctuary Retreat in a home gym. Hose fill, standard outlet, no plumbing. Showroom pricing, and it is running cold on our floor with the saunas next to it.
productBlurbs.summit-ws190: Nobody buys a massage chair from a photo, and the Wellness Shop Summit WS190 is on our floor for exactly that reason: sit in it after a QEW crawl from Mississauga and you will know within five minutes whether it goes home with you. It is the top chair in our own line, built for a daily session in a den or a home office rather than an occasional treat. Pricing is at the showroom, and it pairs naturally with a Sanctuary cabin for a full recovery room.
productBlurbs.dreamcatcher-ws170: Comfortable without taking over the room, the Wellness Shop Dreamcatcher WS170 is the chair we suggest to Tansley Woods retirees who want a nightly massage without giving up the space beside the television. It is the everyday chair in our line, and the honest way to choose is to try it on the floor next to the Summit WS190 and see which one your back prefers; most people know quickly. Pricing is at the showroom, and delivery across Burlington and Halton is part of the conversation.
productBlurbs.duke-series: An enclosed veranda-style cedar gazebo is how a hot tub on Lakeshore Road in Burlington survives the wind off the lake, and the Visscher Duke Series is the one we specify most for that job: Western red cedar, a range of sizes, and walls that turn a November soak into a room. Because it is a permanent structure the city will want to see it on the permit, so plan it with the pad rather than after. Showroom pricing; the size chart and options are at the showroom.
productBlurbs.cypress-series: Privacy is the reason a Dempsey homeowner adds a Visscher Cypress Series gazebo: cedar panels on the sides facing the neighbours, open where the view is, and a roof that keeps snow off the cover so the tub gets used in February. Western red cedar weathers to grey or takes a stain, and the panel design suits the tight rear yards of newer subdivisions where the fence is only six feet from the tub. Pricing is at the showroom and depends on the size and the panel layout you pick.
productBlurbs.hudson-series: Snow up in Kilbride is heavier than it is by the lake, and the Visscher Hudson Series is the enclosed cedar gazebo for a Kilbride tub that has to be usable after a January storm: 11 by 14 and larger, fully enclosed, room for the tub and a bench. Western red cedar throughout. It is also the structure that lets an outdoor sauna and cold plunge routine happen out of the wind. Pricing is at the showroom; bring the tub model so we size the door for delivery.
productBlurbs.sequoia-11-14: Louvers that open for sun and close for rain make the Visscher Sequoia 11 by 14 the gazebo for an Iroquois Ridge deck that faces south and bakes in July. Open-air by design, so a hot tub or a swim spa underneath keeps the outdoor feel while the roof handles weather, and the 11 by 14 footprint clears most seven seat tubs with walking room around them. Western red cedar posts and beams match the fence and the deck. Showroom pricing; ask about the louvered roof options when you visit.
productBlurbs.sedona-9-9: Nine by nine is the smallest Visscher we carry, and the Sedona fits the narrow Milton lot where the tub takes one corner of the yard and the barbecue takes the other. Open-air, so it shades a four to six seat tub without closing in a small space, and the Western red cedar frame goes up on a pad. It is the gazebo for a J-335 or a Nordic round tub rather than a nine seater. Showroom pricing; ask whether your town needs a permit for it.
productBlurbs.savannah-11-11: Square and open, the Visscher Savannah 11 by 11 covers a seven seat tub with room to walk around it, and it suits the deep Aldershot bungalow lots where the tub sits well back from the house and needs its own shelter from the west wind off the harbour. Western red cedar, open-air on all sides, so the view stays. A step up from the Sedona 9 by 9 in cover, it is the one most people pick for a standard rectangular tub. Pricing is at the showroom.

buyCanadian.pageLead: Buying Canadian is about where the money and the responsibility end up. Here the company is based in Ontario, the crew that sets the tub on your pad lives in Halton, and the technician who takes a January call is minutes off the QEW.
body: The Wellness Shop started as a single local hot tub store and has grown over 25 years into eight showrooms across Ontario. Burlington covers Halton and the lakeshore, from Aldershot to Oakville and up the escarpment to Milton, with staff who use the same QEW ramps you do. The sale, the delivery and the warranty work all stay in the province.

The brands are the ones you came in for. We are an authorized Jacuzzi dealer, so every tub carries the full factory warranty. Serenity saunas are built in Canada from Western red cedar. Our Wellness Shop Ontario series was specified for winters on the lake, with full foam insulation and covers that hold up to the wind off the water. Buy Canadian here means choosing where the money and the service live, not giving up the model you wanted.

It pays off after the truck leaves. Cover replacements, filter changes, a pump under warranty: all of it runs through the Burlington showroom with parts on hand and a crew that has already been to your address.

faq.q: Is the Wellness Shop a Canadian company?
faq.a: Yes. The Wellness Shop is 100% Canadian-owned and operated, an Ontario company that started as one local hot tub store and now runs eight showrooms across the province, including the Burlington showroom on the North Service Road. Sales, delivery and service are handled by Ontario staff.

faq.q: Are your hot tubs and saunas Canadian made?
faq.a: Serenity outdoor saunas are built in Canada from Western red cedar. Jacuzzi and our Wellness Shop Ontario series hot tubs are built in the United States, Nordic in Michigan and Aquasolus in Europe. Every one is sold by a Canadian company and delivered and serviced by the Burlington team.
